text:
Forensic findings CASEID
1) Domain context: A generic institutional records office files correspondence into dated, named dossiers, assigns each item a unique identifier, and indexes it by category, counterparty, and date received. Files are retained under fixed retention schedules: active dossiers are kept in the operational store, closed items are moved to archive after an adjudication review, and destruction only occurs once the retention period expires and a destruction log entry is signed off. Auditors access records through a read-only review portal, pull complete file trees by case identifier, and verify integrity via checksums on stored documents. All access events are written to an immutable audit log. Cross-reference is maintained by index links between related items.

2) What occurred: The actor created a private message thread in a direct-messaging channel and exchanged messages with multiple counterpart accounts, each identified only by a named account handle. The actor drafted a shared document, designated with an alphanumeric file identifier, in which the document's "Rate Table" field listed per-property entries with target price values in a currency field, and a "Territory Allocation" section assigned specific neighborhood identifiers to named accounts. The actor attached a second document, a dated record with a "Penalty Schedule" section, enumerating named accounts in a "Non-compliant Parties" field and corresponding escalation actions in an "Enforcement Steps" field. The actor used an end-to-end encrypted messaging channel for subsequent coordination, and a scheduling application entry with the subject line "Sync" was created, with attendee fields populated with the same named accounts. The actor then sent an outbound email from a named account to each counterpart, with the subject line "Q3 Update" and an attachment reference to the shared document's file identifier.

3) Materials/access observed: The actor accessed the shared document store and the scheduling application from the same IP address range associated with the named account. The end-to-end encrypted channel metadata included device identifiers and a key-exchange timestamp. The audit log recorded three read events on the Penalty Schedule document by accounts other than the originating named account.

4) Indicators & artifacts: A dated record with a "Territory Allocation" section mapping neighborhood identifiers to named accounts; a shared document with a "Rate Table" field containing synchronized target price values across multiple named accounts; a "Penalty Schedule" document with a "Non-compliant Parties" field populated with named accounts and escalation actions in an "Enforcement Steps" field; end-to-end encrypted message threads between multiple named accounts discussing coordination; a scheduling entry with "Sync" in the subject line and matching attendee fields; an outbound email from a named account with subject line "Q3 Update" referencing the shared document's file identifier; and audit-log entries showing cross-account read access to the Penalty Schedule document.
